title: TENET: plain color, connected motion
question: A fresh set built around interaction, not decorative styling. The images are static; each direction describes the animation it would use.

options.label: 01 · Sequence
options.thesis: Browse calls as a contact sheet; the selected record expands into a full-width visual explanation.
options.viewport: A broad visual explanation above a horizontal strip of recent calls. No permanent sidebar.
options.risk: The contact sheet needs a compact list alternative for sessions with many calls.
options.case: Motion: the selected call expands from its thumbnail; changing calls slides the selection once, while shared elements stay anchored.

raised.raise: Keep positions stable while values change.
Use a single continuous selection movement, not animation on every component.
Make every call a recognisable object without decorative mascots.
Keep the selected record visible in its session context.
Keep most of the screen achromatic; selection alone owns color.

options.label: 02 · Focus
options.thesis: A call list opens into one attached inspection sheet, making context and detail feel like the same object.
options.viewport: A compact call list stays visible while its selected row grows into a large white reading sheet.
options.risk: A familiar master-detail pattern; its distinction depends on the quality of the shared-element transition.
options.case: Motion: the selected row becomes the sheet header; a rule opens its evidence in place, and closing returns to exactly the same row.

options.label: 03 · Decision map
options.lineage: Tensegrity diagrams, translated into a flat recorded-gate graph
options.thesis: Show exactly which recorded check contributed to the decision as a connected diagram.
options.viewport: A large diagram connects command, rule outcome, confidence gate and policy result. Actual execution is separate and explicitly explained by observe mode.
options.risk: The graph must contain recorded gates only; it must never invent evaluator reasoning or imply an execution block that did not occur.
options.case: Stronger at visually explaining recorded gate contributions, less familiar for browsing many calls. Motion: selecting a gate traces its existing connection once and opens its evidence beside it.

options.label: Seven-segment displays
options.thesis: Fixed cells make changing values legible.
options.viewport: Exact confidence numbers in fixed positions.
options.case: Weaker on developer identification and on explaining the decision.

options.label: Emission-line rail
options.thesis: The selected record opens from a continuous calibrated rail.
options.viewport: One expanded record sits above a line of ticks.
options.risk: Tiny line-only labels make calls too hard to identify.
options.case: Weaker on both audience identification and immediate comprehension.

options.label: Character roster
options.viewport: A call grid expands the selected record.
options.risk: Personifying decisions suggests reliability or intention not present in the data.
options.case: Weaker on both audience identification and product clarity.

options.label: Orienteering map
options.thesis: Keep a selected record and its session position visible together.
options.risk: A navigable route can falsely imply a required order or causal relationship.
options.case: Weaker on developer identification and truthful explanation than a contact sheet.
options.kept: A persistent indication of the selected record's context.

options.label: Cloud edge
options.thesis: Nearly achromatic reading with an active edge.
options.viewport: One highlighted boundary indicates the selected region.
options.risk: Iridescent material conflicts with the requested plain colors.
options.case: Weaker on both audience identification and product clarity.
options.kept: Most of the screen stays achromatic.
